subject: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway 40B Comprehensive Permit
overview: The Board reviewed updated traffic and architectural plans for a proposed 350-unit residential development, focusing on building setbacks, bicycle storage, and pedestrian safety. The hearing was continued to March 30, 2023, to address procedural requirements regarding the expiration of state remote meeting authorizations.

items.title: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway (Case 40B-2022-01)
items.summary: The Board resumed consideration of a comprehensive permit petition for a 350-unit multifamily development consisting of two eight-story buildings.

items.title: Traffic Peer Review Response
items.summary: Andrew Arsenault presented updated traffic volume data and addressed peer review comments concerning vehicle turning radii in the parking garage and pedestrian sight distances.

items.title: Bicycle Storage and Parking Analysis
items.summary: Board members questioned the adequacy of bicycle storage and suggested removing difficult parking stalls to avoid atypical backing maneuvers, leading the applicant to increase the bike space count to 96.

items.title: Architectural and Landscape Revisions
items.summary: The applicant presented building revisions including recessed balconies to improve facade articulation and increased sidewalk buffers on Commercial Street to accommodate larger shade trees.

items.title: Amenity Spaces and Play Areas
items.summary: The Board discussed replacing a traditional playground with flexible 'adventure play' equipment in a residential courtyard and the addition of a new rooftop deck.

items.title: Peer Reviewer and Consultant Feedback
items.summary: Architectural consultant Cliff Bomer expressed support for the facade improvements but encouraged further building setbacks and the use of high-quality cementitious materials.

items.title: Meeting Schedule and Continuance
items.summary: Approved continuing the hearing to March 30, 2023, as a procedural measure to ensure meeting continuity pending a state extension of remote meeting laws.
